exploit_name: Epoch-boundary checkpoints retroactively qualify for previous epoch rewards
description: epochTimestampEnd(n) returns the first timestamp of epoch n+1, not the last moment of epoch n. Combined with inclusive checkpoint lookups (ts <= t) in VotingEscrow, positions created at the boundary are counted in the previous epoch's reward distribution despite not participating.
attack_scenario: 1) Attacker waits until t = epochTimestampEnd(prevEpoch). 2) currentEpoch() already returns prevEpoch + 1. 3) Attacker creates a fresh lock with maximum duration. 4) claimRewards() for prevEpoch includes the new checkpoint with zero decay. 5) Attacker receives full epoch emissions for zero participation.
root_cause: epochTimestampEnd(n) returns the first timestamp of epoch n+1, not the last moment of epoch n. Combined with inclusive checkpoint lookups (ts <= t) in VotingEscrow, positions created at the boundary are counted in the previous epoch's reward distribution despite not participating.
fix_description: Make epoch-end snapshots exclusive by snapshotting at epochTimestampEnd(epoch) - 1 to exclude boundary-second positions, or redefine epoch-end helpers to use inclusive in-epoch timestamps consistently.
notes: Direct reward theft. Attacker can join at epoch boundary, capture pro-rata rewards for an epoch they never participated in. If no other participants existed, attacker captures entire epoch emissions.
